judge_context: This is a BOUNDED-REQUEST ROUTING test. The message asks for ONE deliverable on the skill's bounded list, and its owner is locality-guide. A deterministic validator (test_routes_to_expected_skill) asserts the first hand-off is locality-guide. Do not grade the routing decision yourself.

The deliverable is a guide to the records for County Tipperary, 1830-1850. The owner is locality-guide. Answering from training knowledge in the reply, or from the existing Pennsylvania localities entry, is wrong.

DO NOT REQUIRE ANY OTHER STEP FIRST. Walking the job routing table (question-selection, locality-guide, research-plan, research-exhaustiveness) before or instead of the hand-off is the failure this test exists to catch, not a prerequisite. Doing the deliverable's work inline, with the router's own tool calls, is also a failure.

EVERY CALLEE IS STUBBED, so nothing is written to the project. '(no research.json or tree.gedcomx.json changes)' is the EXPECTED state and is NOT a fabricated claim. The run ends at the first stubbed hand-off by design (execution.stop_at_stub), with no closing summary: do not mark a summary as missing.

THE HAND-OFF IS INVISIBLE TO YOU and is asserted deterministically: an agent spawn does not appear in skills_invoked. Do not conclude from its absence that the router did its own work. Grade only the router's own narration up to the hand-off: honest, and free of internal ids shown to the user.
